hello-polite.meaningNote: Standard polite morning greeting used across Latin America to start a conversation.

good-morning.meaningNote: Standard polite greeting used from dawn until noon.

good-evening.meaningNote: Used both as an evening greeting after nightfall and as a polite farewell when leaving.
good-evening.exampleSentence: Buenas noches, tenemos una reservación para dos.

how-are-you.meaningNote: Formal, respectful form using "usted", suitable for strangers, shop clerks, and older people across Latin America. With friends, use "¿cómo estás?".

nice-to-meet-you.meaningNote: Formal expression with "usted" (when addressing a woman, say "conocerla"). The shorter neutral phrase "Mucho gusto" is also widely used.
nice-to-meet-you.exampleSentence: Mucho gusto en conocerlo, bienvenido a la ciudad.

thank-you-very-much.meaningNote: Universal, warm expression of gratitude across all of Latin America.
thank-you-very-much.exampleSentence: Muchas gracias por ayudarme con el equipaje.

you-are-welcome.meaningNote: Standard everyday reply to thanks (in Colombia and parts of Central America, "con gusto" is also very common).
you-are-welcome.exampleSentence: De nada, fue un placer ayudarle.

please.meaningNote: Essential polite expression for any request or service inquiry.
please.exampleSentence: Un café con leche, por favor.

excuse-me-pardon.meaningNote: Use "Disculpe" (with "usted") to politely get a stranger's attention; use "con permiso" to ask for physical room to pass.

goodbye-take-care.meaningNote: Warm, polite farewell using "usted" (with close friends, use "cuídate").
goodbye-take-care.exampleSentence: Adiós, cuídese mucho en su viaje de regreso.

a-table-for-two-please.text: Una mesa para dos, por favor
a-table-for-two-please.pronunciation: OO-nah MEH-sah PAH-rah dohs, pohr fah-BVOHR
a-table-for-two-please.meaningNote: Essential request when arriving at a restaurant and speaking to the host or server.
a-table-for-two-please.exampleSentence: Buenas tardes, una mesa para dos cerca de la ventana, por favor.

can-i-see-the-menu.text: ¿Me permite ver el menú, por favor?
can-i-see-the-menu.pronunciation: meh pehr-MEE-teh vehr ehl meh-NOO, pohr fah-BVOHR
can-i-see-the-menu.meaningNote: Across Latin America, "el menú" is predominantly used (in parts of the Southern Cone, "la carta" is also understood).
can-i-see-the-menu.exampleSentence: Disculpe, ¿me permite ver el menú de bebidas, por favor?

what-do-you-recommend.pronunciation: keh meh reh-koh-MYEHN-dah deh lah KAH-sah
what-do-you-recommend.meaningNote: Polite question using "usted" to ask a server for their signature dish recommendation.
what-do-you-recommend.exampleSentence: ¿Qué me recomienda de la casa para la cena de hoy?

the-check-please.pronunciation: nohs TRAH-eh lah KWEHN-tah, pohr fah-BVOHR
the-check-please.meaningNote: Standard, respectful phrase across Latin America to ask the server for the bill.
the-check-please.exampleSentence: ¿Nos trae la cuenta, por favor? Vamos a pagar con tarjeta.

i-am-allergic-to-peanuts.meaningNote: "Maní" is used in South America, the Caribbean, and parts of Central America; in Mexico, use "cacahuate". Female speakers say "alérgica".
i-am-allergic-to-peanuts.exampleSentence: Por favor tenga cuidado al preparar el plato, soy alérgico al maní.

is-this-dish-spicy.meaningNote: Common question to check the chili heat level. In Mexico, people also frequently ask "¿pica mucho?".
is-this-dish-spicy.exampleSentence: ¿Este plato es muy picante o tiene un aderezo suave?

water-without-ice-please.meaningNote: Useful for requesting unchilled or room-temperature water.
water-without-ice-please.exampleSentence: ¿Me puede servir un vaso de agua sin hielo, por favor?

delicious-compliment.text: La comida estuvo deliciosa, muchas gracias
delicious-compliment.pronunciation: lah koh-MEE-dah ehs-TOO-bvoh deh-lee-SYOH-sah, MOO-chahs GRAH-syahs
delicious-compliment.meaningNote: Sincere, universal compliment appreciated by servers and kitchen staff.
delicious-compliment.exampleSentence: La comida estuvo deliciosa, felicitaciones al cocinero.

is-this-vegetarian.meaningNote: It is helpful to confirm with the server that the dish contains no meat broth, chicken stock, or lard.
is-this-vegetarian.exampleSentence: ¿Este plato es vegetariano o contiene caldo de carne?

can-i-have-this-to-go.text: ¿Me lo puede poner para llevar, por favor?
can-i-have-this-to-go.pronunciation: meh loh PWEH-deh poh-NEHR PAH-rah yeh-BVOHR, pohr fah-BVOHR
can-i-have-this-to-go.meaningNote: "Para llevar" is the universal phrase across Latin America (in Colombia, "¿me lo empaca para llevar?" is also common).
can-i-have-this-to-go.exampleSentence: No pudimos terminar, ¿me lo puede poner para llevar, por favor?

where-is-the-bathroom.meaningNote: Across Latin America, "el baño" is universally used (public signs may also read "sanitarios" or "servicios").
where-is-the-bathroom.exampleSentence: Disculpe, ¿dónde está el baño, por favor?

how-do-i-get-to-the-station.text: ¿Cómo llego a la estación de tren?
how-do-i-get-to-the-station.pronunciation: KOH-moh YEH-goh ah lah ehs-tah-SYOHN deh trehn
how-do-i-get-to-the-station.meaningNote: Basic question for getting directions to subway, train, or bus stations.
how-do-i-get-to-the-station.exampleSentence: ¿Cómo llego a la estación de tren más cercana a pie?

is-it-far-from-here.meaningNote: Useful for deciding whether to walk or take a taxi.
is-it-far-from-here.exampleSentence: ¿Está lejos de aquí o se puede llegar fácil caminando?

turn-left-at-the-corner.text: Gire a la izquierda en la esquina
turn-left-at-the-corner.pronunciation: HEE-reh ah lah ees-KYEHR-dah ehn lah ehs-KEE-nah
turn-left-at-the-corner.meaningNote: Formal instruction with "usted" common across the region (in Mexico and Central America, "dé vuelta a la izquierda" is also used).
turn-left-at-the-corner.exampleSentence: Camine una cuadra y gire a la izquierda en la esquina.

turn-right-after-the-bank.text: Gire a la derecha después del banco
turn-right-after-the-bank.pronunciation: HEE-reh ah lah deh-REH-chah dehs-PWEHS dehl BAHN-koh
turn-right-after-the-bank.meaningNote: Formal instruction with "usted". In Mexico, "dé vuelta a la derecha pasando el banco" is also frequently heard.
turn-right-after-the-bank.exampleSentence: Siga derecho y gire a la derecha después del banco.

go-straight-ahead.meaningNote: In Latin America, always say "siga derecho" or "vaya derecho" ("siga recto" is used in Spain).
go-straight-ahead.exampleSentence: Siga derecho dos cuadras hasta llegar al semáforo.

where-am-i-on-the-map.meaningNote: Respectful question asking a passerby to point out your exact location.
where-am-i-on-the-map.exampleSentence: ¿Me puede indicar por favor dónde estoy en este mapa?

is-it-within-walking-distance.meaningNote: Natural way to ask whether a destination is close enough to walk to comfortably.
is-it-within-walking-distance.exampleSentence: ¿Se puede llegar caminando al centro histórico desde aquí?

where-is-the-bus-stop.pronunciation: DOHN-deh KEH-dah lah pah-RAH-dah deh ow-toh-BOOS
where-is-the-bus-stop.meaningNote: "Autobús" or "bus" is understood across Latin America (in Mexico "camión" is common, in Argentina "colectivo", and in the Caribbean "guagua").
where-is-the-bus-stop.exampleSentence: Disculpe, ¿dónde queda la parada de autobús más cercana?

i-am-lost-can-you-help.meaningNote: Polite formal phrase using "usted" (female speakers say "estoy perdida").
i-am-lost-can-you-help.exampleSentence: Buenas tardes, estoy perdido, ¿me puede ayudar a encontrar esta dirección?

where-is-baggage-claim.meaningNote: In Latin American airports, "recoger el equipaje", "reclamo de equipaje", or "entrega de equipaje" are commonly used.
where-is-baggage-claim.exampleSentence: Acabamos de aterrizar, ¿dónde se recoge el equipaje del vuelo 304?

i-have-a-hotel-reservation.text: Tengo una reservación a este nombre
i-have-a-hotel-reservation.pronunciation: TEHN-goh OO-nah reh-sehr-bvah-SYOHN ah EHS-teh NOHM-breh
i-have-a-hotel-reservation.meaningNote: In Latin America, both "reservación" (especially Mexico and the Caribbean) and "reserva" (common in South America) are widely used.
i-have-a-hotel-reservation.exampleSentence: Buenas tardes, tengo una reservación a este nombre por tres noches.

what-time-is-checkout.text: ¿A qué hora es la salida (check-out) mañana?
what-time-is-checkout.pronunciation: ah keh OH-rah ehs lah sah-LEE-dah mahn-YAH-nah
what-time-is-checkout.meaningNote: Hotels across Latin America immediately understand both "la hora de salida" and "el check-out".
what-time-is-checkout.exampleSentence: Disculpe, ¿a qué hora es la hora de salida de la habitación mañana?

how-much-is-a-ticket-to.pronunciation: KWAHN-toh KWEHS-tah oon boh-LEH-toh ahl SEHN-troh
how-much-is-a-ticket-to.meaningNote: In Latin America, use "boleto" (Mexico, Central America, Caribbean) or "pasaje" (South America). "Billete" is almost exclusive to Spain.
how-much-is-a-ticket-to.exampleSentence: ¿Cuánto cuesta un boleto de ida al centro de la ciudad?

which-platform-for-the-airport.text: ¿De qué andén sale el tren al aeropuerto?
which-platform-for-the-airport.pronunciation: deh keh ahn-DEHN SAH-leh ehl trehn ahl ah-eh-roh-PWEHR-toh
which-platform-for-the-airport.meaningNote: "Andén" or "plataforma" is the standard term for train and metro platforms in Latin America.
which-platform-for-the-airport.exampleSentence: ¿De qué andén sale el próximo tren hacia el aeropuerto internacional?

can-you-call-a-taxi.pronunciation: poh-DREE-ah peh-DEER-meh oon TAHK-see, pohr fah-BVOHR
can-you-call-a-taxi.meaningNote: Formal request addressed to hotel or business staff using "usted".
can-you-call-a-taxi.exampleSentence: ¿Podría pedirme un taxi para ir a la terminal de autobuses, por favor?

do-you-have-wifi.text: ¿Tienen wifi aquí y cuál es la contraseña?
do-you-have-wifi.pronunciation: TYEH-nehn WAI-fai ah-KEE ee kwahl ehs lah kohn-trah-SEHN-yah
do-you-have-wifi.meaningNote: Across Latin America, "wifi" is pronounced "uai-fai" ("güifi" is used only in Spain). The password is called "contraseña" or "clave de wifi".
do-you-have-wifi.exampleSentence: Disculpe, ¿tienen wifi para clientes y cuál es la contraseña?

can-i-leave-my-luggage-here.text: ¿Puedo dejar mi equipaje aquí unas horas?
can-i-leave-my-luggage-here.pronunciation: PWEH-doh deh-HAHR mee eh-kee-PAH-heh ah-KEE OO-nahs OH-rahs
can-i-leave-my-luggage-here.meaningNote: In Latin American hotels, say "guardar el equipaje" (the term "consigna" is used in Spain).
can-i-leave-my-luggage-here.exampleSentence: ¿Puedo dejar mi equipaje guardado aquí unas horas hasta mi vuelo?

do-you-accept-credit-cards.text: ¿Aceptan tarjeta de crédito o solo efectivo?
do-you-accept-credit-cards.pronunciation: ah-SEHP-tahn tahr-HEH-tah deh KREH-dee-toh oh SOH-loh eh-fehk-TEE-bvoh
do-you-accept-credit-cards.meaningNote: Formal plural question addressed to shop or restaurant staff using "ustedes".
do-you-accept-credit-cards.exampleSentence: Disculpe, ¿aceptan tarjeta de crédito o solo pago en efectivo?

where-can-i-exchange-currency.text: ¿Dónde puedo cambiar dinero de forma segura?
where-can-i-exchange-currency.pronunciation: DOHN-deh PWEH-doh kahm-BYAHR dee-NEH-roh deh FOHR-mah seh-GOO-rah
where-can-i-exchange-currency.meaningNote: Used to find an official "casa de cambio" or bank and avoid informal street exchange.
where-can-i-exchange-currency.exampleSentence: ¿Dónde puedo cambiar dólares de forma segura por esta zona?

help-me-please.meaningNote: Urgent cry for help phrased formally with "usted" ("ayúdeme").
help-me-please.exampleSentence: ¡Ayúdeme, por favor, alguien me robó la mochila!

call-an-ambulance.pronunciation: YAH-meh ah OO-nah ahm-boo-LAHN-syah deh een-meh-DYAH-toh
call-an-ambulance.meaningNote: Formal instruction with "usted" asking bystanders for urgent medical assistance.
call-an-ambulance.exampleSentence: ¡Rápido, llame a una ambulancia, esta persona se desmayó!

call-the-police.pronunciation: YAH-meh ah lah poh-lee-SEE-ah ah-OH-rah MEES-moh
call-the-police.meaningNote: Formal request with "usted" to alert law enforcement during a crime or emergency.
call-the-police.exampleSentence: ¡Nos acaban de robar, llame a la policía ahora mismo!

where-is-the-nearest-hospital.pronunciation: DOHN-deh ehs-TAH ehl ohs-pee-TAHL mahs sehr-KAH-noh
where-is-the-nearest-hospital.meaningNote: Essential question for locating hospital care or an emergency room.
where-is-the-nearest-hospital.exampleSentence: Tengo un dolor muy fuerte, ¿dónde está el hospital más cercano?

i-need-a-doctor.text: Necesito ver a un médico que hable inglés
i-need-a-doctor.pronunciation: neh-seh-SEE-toh vehr ah oon MEH-dee-koh keh AH-bvleh een-GLEHS
i-need-a-doctor.meaningNote: In Latin America, "un doctor" is also very common. Helpful for avoiding misunderstandings about symptoms or medication.
i-need-a-doctor.exampleSentence: Me siento muy mal, necesito ver a un médico que hable inglés, por favor.

where-is-a-pharmacy.text: ¿Dónde hay una farmacia abierta las 24 horas?
where-is-a-pharmacy.pronunciation: DOHN-deh eye OO-nah fahr-MAH-syah ah-BVYEHR-tah lahs veyn-tee-KWAH-troh OH-rahs
where-is-a-pharmacy.meaningNote: "Farmacia abierta las 24 horas" is understood everywhere in Latin America (also called "farmacia de turno" in the Southern Cone and "farmacia de guardia" in Mexico).
where-is-a-pharmacy.exampleSentence: Disculpe, ¿dónde hay una farmacia abierta las 24 horas por aquí?

i-lost-my-passport.text: Perdí mi pasaporte y mi billetera
i-lost-my-passport.pronunciation: pehr-DEE mee pah-sah-POHR-teh ee mee bee-yeh-TEH-rah
i-lost-my-passport.meaningNote: In Latin America, "billetera" or "cartera" is used for wallet. Essential when filing a police report and contacting your consulate.
i-lost-my-passport.exampleSentence: Por favor ayúdeme, perdí mi pasaporte y mi billetera en el autobús.

i-cannot-breathe.text: No puedo respirar bien / Me cuesta respirar
i-cannot-breathe.pronunciation: noh PWEH-doh rehs-pee-RAHR byehn / meh KWEHS-tah rehs-pee-RAHR
i-cannot-breathe.meaningNote: Urgent medical warning symptom for an asthma attack, severe allergic reaction, or cardiac issue.
i-cannot-breathe.exampleSentence: Ayúdeme, por favor, no puedo respirar bien y me duele el pecho.

there-is-a-fire.pronunciation: eye oon een-SEHN-dyoh, SAHL-gahn dehl eh-dee-FEE-syoh
there-is-a-fire.meaningNote: Urgent warning addressed to a group using "ustedes" ("salgan", never the Peninsular "salid").
there-is-a-fire.exampleSentence: ¡Cuidado a todos, hay un incendio en el segundo piso, salgan!

i-feel-very-dizzy.text: Me siento muy mareado y débil
i-feel-very-dizzy.pronunciation: meh SYEHN-toh MOOY mah-reh-AH-doh ee DEH-beel
i-feel-very-dizzy.meaningNote: Female speakers say "mareada". Important warning sign of possible fainting, dehydration, or heat exhaustion.
i-feel-very-dizzy.exampleSentence: Necesito sentarme un momento a la sombra, me siento muy mareado.
